thread.title: Senate passes Laughlin bill to expand awareness of LIFE Program for seniors
thread.title_full: Senate passes Laughlin bill to expand awareness of LIFE Program for seniors

author: w. k. barton
title: Senate passes Laughlin bill to expand awareness of LIFE Program for seniors
text:
Legislation sponsored by Senator Dan Laughlin to improve outreach and accountability for Pennsylvania’s Living Independence for the Elderly (LIFE) Program passed the Pennsylvania Senate on June 24.
Senate Bill 482 aims to ensure that older Pennsylvanians receive comprehensive information about long-term care options, specifically focusing on the LIFE Program, which assists eligible seniors in remaining in their homes and communities while receiving healthcare and support services. Laughlin said, “Many seniors and their families are simply unaware that the LIFE Program exists or that they may qualify for it. This bill is about making sure older Pennsylvanians have access to all available options before making important decisions about their long-term care.”
Currently, individuals enrolling in Medicaid managed care may not be informed about the LIFE Program during enrollment. The legislation requires the state’s Independent Enrollment Broker to include details about the program in materials provided to eligible individuals. Additionally, it establishes quarterly reporting requirements to verify compliance and ensure information reaches those who qualify. The bill also permits sharing necessary information with LIFE providers so they can determine eligibility and connect individuals with appropriate services.
Laughlin said, “For many seniors, remaining independent and living in their own home is critical to their quality of life. This legislation promotes informed choice, strengthens transparency, and helps ensure seniors can make decisions based on a full understanding of the services available to them.” The LIFE Program serves adults who qualify for nursing facility-level care but prefer independent living with community-based support.
SB 482 now moves forward to consideration by the Pennsylvania House of Representatives.
According to the official website of Senator Dan Laughlin, he secured investments such as more than $3 million in state tax credits for Erie County organizations, $10 million for water infrastructure improvements, $13.4 million in federal broadband funding; maintained offices in Harrisburg and Erie; focused on policies generating employment while curbing government spending; served as chair of the Senate Law and Justice Committee; grew up in Erie as son of a World War II veteran before becoming a small business owner; and represented nearly all of Erie County including its city along with numerous townships and boroughs.
